binders: Implicit real parameters K (bulkModulus) and rho (density).
A system carrying real-valued pressure p(x,t) and velocity u(x,t) and the pointwise equations encoded by its type.
hypotheses: By the system structure, rho != 0 and at every (x,t) the fields have partial derivatives satisfying p_t+K*u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)*p_x=0.
conclusions: For w=p+rho*c*u and every x,t, temporal and spatial derivatives w_t,w_x exist at (x,t) and satisfy w_t+c*w_x=0.
mathematical_definitions: c is the principal nonnegative real square root sqrt(K/rho).
The pointwise transport predicate q_t+s*q_x=0 includes existence of the indicated one-variable derivatives with the other coordinate fixed.
The system type packages p,u and pointwise derivative witnesses satisfying the two first-order equations.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive real bulk modulus K and density rho and every packaged solution (p,u) of p_t+K u_x=0 and u_t+(1/rho)p_x=0, the speed c=sqrt(K/rho) is positive, and the right-mode variable w=p+rho*c*u satisfies w_t+c w_x=0 at every point.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result is restricted to strictly positive real K and rho; the system structure also carries rho != 0.
All PDE assertions are pointwise and express partial derivatives using one-variable HasDerivAt predicates.
The theorem quantifies over an already-packaged system, so the universal claim would be vacuous if no such system existed; constant zero fields give an evident compatible example for nonzero rho.
The conclusion does not give a global profile representation w=f(x-c*t), initial or boundary conditions, uniqueness, or regularity beyond the displayed pointwise first derivatives.
The positive-speed conclusion is explicit and is conjoined with, rather than assumed by, the transport conclusion.
